lessons: Skill verified in excellent shape: all 9 hardcoded 2026 Jewish-holiday Gregorian dates match hebcal.com exactly (zero off-by-one); all named media outlets (Geektime, Calcalist/Calcalist Tech, CTech, The Marker, Globes, Ynet Tech, No Camels, Walla Tech) operate in 2026 and are accurately described; the AEO/AI-search section is current and well-grounded (~82% of AI citations are earned media); the >70% mobile-first stat is conservative.

MAJOR fixed: content_planner.py holiday table ended at 2026, so the forward-planning tool returned an empty calendar for 2027 (it is mid-2026). Added a verified 2027 block (cross-checked against hebcal: Purim 03-23, Pesach 04-22, Yom HaZikaron 05-11, Yom Ha'atzmaut 05-12, Shavuot 06-11, Rosh Hashana 10-02, Yom Kippur 10-11, Sukkot 10-16, Hanukkah 12-25 first full day), and updated the SKILL.md/HE notes to '2025, 2026, 2027'. Add 2028 next cycle.
Fixed MINOR: docstring referenced the old name 'JEWISH_HOLIDAYS' (actual dict is JEWISH_HOLIDAYS_BY_YEAR).

CRITICAL fixed (Expert): Yom HaShoah (Holocaust Remembrance Day) was entirely absent, a major miss for a skill that exists to prevent tone-deaf commercial posting (it is one of Israel's two siren / advertising-suspension solemn days). Added it to the planner for all 3 years (2025-04-24, 2026-04-14, 2027-05-04, verified vs hebcal), to NO_COMMERCIAL_DAYS, and to the 'absolute no-commercial-content days' line in SKILL.md + SKILL_HE.md.

MAJOR fixed (Expert): the planner modeled multi-day holidays as single dates, contradicting the skill's own week-long-slowdown prose. Added a duration field per holiday (Pesach 7, Sukkot 7, Hanukkah 8, Rosh Hashana 2) so the calendar renders the full avoid-window and catches holidays whose window spills into the queried month.

Fixed a PRE-EXISTING date error surfaced while rewriting: the 2025 rows had Yom HaZikaron 04-25 / Yom Ha'atzmaut 04-26, but hebcal shows 2025-04-30 / 2025-05-01 (the original was ~5 days off). Corrected.
Fixed: the Chok HaSpam evidence source_url (gov.il/legalInfo/spam_law) now 403s; swapped to the kolzchut spam-law page.

Deferred (MINOR): add 2028 holiday rows; optionally add Tu BiShvat / Lag BaOmer / Tisha B'Av (Tisha B'Av is a low-commercial-sensitivity day worth flagging); note CTech's live English site is calcalistech.com; reconcile the Times-of-Israel / Walla asymmetry between SKILL.md body and the reference file; consider softening the AEO earned-media claim to 'tend to favor'.

CRITICAL dead outlet: the skill routed English-language PR pitches to NoCamels in three places (SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md, references/israeli-media-landscape.md). NoCamels CEASED operations: its About page says it was active 2011-2024 and that operations are paused, and its last post is 31 October 2024, roughly 22 months before this cycle. Verified with a bogus-path negative control on the same host.

CRITICAL false clearance in the PRIOR optimization log: v1.2.0 recorded that 'all named media outlets ... operate in 2026 and are accurately described', naming No Camels explicitly. It had already been dark for ~20 months. Whatever entity check ran that cycle did not fetch the outlets. Every outlet is now individually fetched, and references/israeli-media-landscape.md gained Status and Last verified columns so the next cycle cannot repeat this.

CRITICAL inert evidence: the evidence entry israeli-tech-media-outlets asserted the status of EIGHT outlets while citing a single Geektime AI category page, which cannot support a claim about any of the other seven. Similarly israel-mobile-first-70 had verified_via 'claim about the source itself; snippet is the cited page's own title', i.e. it confirmed a DataReportal page EXISTED and never that it said >70%. That is precisely how a wrong number passes a green gate.

COHORT DEFECT CONFIRMED: '>70% mobile' appeared in 4 places (EN and HE body plus both Gotchas). This is the same figure israeli-paid-ads corrected in this same batch. StatCounter July 2026 has Israel at 53.62% mobile / 44.91% desktop, verified independently at the source rather than taken from the sibling skill. The claim was not merely stale, it drove the advice: the Gotcha told agents that desktop-shaped content 'performs poorly', when nearly half the audience is on desktop.

MAJOR wrong destination: 'Ynet Tech' does not exist. ynet.co.il/tech returns 404; the section is ynet.co.il/digital. Confirmed against a bogus-path control on the same host. Present in both skill files and the reference table.

SCRIPT BUG (found by running it, not by reading it): content_planner.py filtered holidays with `start.month == args.month or end.month == args.month`, comparing month with no year. An 8-day Hanukkah starting 25 December ends in the FOLLOWING January, so `--month 1 --year 2027` reported '2027-12-25 to 2028-01-01: Hanukkah' for a January that had no holiday. Fixed by comparing (year, month) tuples, and regression-tested in both directions. The hardcoded date TABLES for 2025, 2026 and 2027 were separately verified against hebcal and are all correct.

CROSS-FILE CONTRADICTION: SKILL.md Troubleshooting said peak times '8-9am and 12-1pm' while the bundled script's defaults are 09:00-10:00, 12:00-13:00 and 19:00-21:00, and the skill omitted the evening slot entirely. Neither was sourced. Reconciled to the script's values and relabelled as starting defaults to be replaced by the account's own analytics.

COMPLIANCE HOLE: Chok HaSpam appeared only as the parenthetical 'email newsletter (Chok HaSpam compliant)' in a skill whose entire output is mass distribution. Added a Distribution Compliance section in both languages with the operative rules: prior consent required, up to NIS 1,000 per message with no proof of damage and awards accumulating, criminal liability up to NIS 226,000 (2026), same-channel opt-out, consent records. Also added the disclosure duty for paid or group-seeded content and a pointer to Amendment 13 for list building, since the skill instructs both.

MAJOR unsupported claim: the Reference Links table advertised Geektime as offering 'guest post opportunities'. Its site offers a commercial 'פרסמו אצלנו' route and general contact, not a documented editorial guest-contributor programme. Reworded, with the note that a paid placement is not a guest post and must be labelled.

STALE terminology, EN only: Example 2 said 'LinkedIn and Twitter' while the Hebrew file already said X. A prior cycle updated one language and not the other. Same class as the InMail-to-Sponsored-Messaging drift the sibling skill found.

Hebrew naturalness: 'מדיה מורווחת' (a calque of earned media that reads as 'spaced out'), 'ספריות אמינות' (ספרייה is a library, not a directory), 'תקצירי AI' (Google's Hebrew surface says סקירות AI) and 'זה מוריד אות הבחנה' were all corrected. Notable because the skill's own Gotcha warns that machine-translated Hebrew makes Israeli audiences disengage.

Unsourced quantitative claims relabelled rather than deleted: the H2-every-200-300-words and 2-3-sentence-paragraph rules are now stated as editorial conventions, not published ranking thresholds, and the AEO section's Hebrew-underrepresentation premise is stated as a working assumption to check per topic rather than a measured fact.

Added deliberate crawler-permission guidance (Google-Extended) to the AEO section, which previously told the reader how to get cited by AI without mentioning the setting that decides whether they can be.

Deferred (MAJOR, next cycle): no measurement layer at all (no KPIs, GSC/GA4, or way to tell whether the calendar worked) in a skill that plans and distributes; no Arabic- or Russian-language lane despite the skill being named for the Israeli market; PR mechanics (embargoes, exclusives, release vs pitch) absent, and the 'WhatsApp follow-ups acceptable' claim carries no source or frequency limit; hreflang/he-IL is one Troubleshooting line despite bilingual strategy being in the description; the EN body outlet list still omits Walla Tech while the reference file lists it.
Phase 5.7 not run: the description and trigger surface were unchanged.
